claim_text: Samsung says a third-party vendor that handled advertising data for Samsung Ads North America was involved in a cyber incident
summary: A Samsung spokesperson said the company knows of a cyber incident at a third-party vendor that supported advertising data processing for Samsung Ads North America. Early findings say some Samsung information may have been affected.
detail: Samsung gave the same statement to Cybernews and, separately, to the Korean outlet DailySecu. Android Headlines repeats Cybernews. We found no Samsung newsroom page with it. Samsung does not name the vendor, say how it happened or what was taken.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Samsung's own statement to two independent outlets (Cybernews and DailySecu); no company page exists to cite.

claim_text: A ransomware group called n0n says it stole the data and published about 220MB of it
summary: Cybernews reports that the group n0n posted about 220MB of data it says belongs to Samsung, after a countdown ran out. DailySecu reported the group listing Samsung as a victim on Nov 14, per a threat-intel service.
detail: We did not look at the leak page. Android Headlines repeats Cybernews. DailySecu says it was not confirmed whether the claimed data came from Samsung itself or a partner. Samsung's statement does not name the group.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Reported by Cybernews and DailySecu; the group's own post is not cited.

claim_text: About 150,000 smart TV viewing events from 2024 were in the dump, with timestamps, viewing time, device details, city, ZIP code and TV provider, but not what was watched
summary: Cybernews researchers say one set holds about 150,000 viewing events from 2024: timestamp, viewing time, device information, city, ZIP code and TV provider name. Cybernews says it does not show what viewers watched.
detail: Android Headlines repeats the figures. These are the outlet's description of the files; Samsung has not confirmed the contents.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cybernews researchers examined the files; Samsung has not confirmed the contents.

claim_text: About 42,600 political advertising records from Sept to Oct 2026 were in the dump
summary: Cybernews says another set holds about 42,600 records on political ads aired between September and October 2026, with political affiliations, issues, sponsors, estimated costs and timestamps, plus one political ad video.
detail: These are ad-business records, not viewer records, per Cybernews. Android Headlines repeats the figure.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cybernews researchers examined the files; Samsung has not confirmed the contents.

claim_text: About 99,100 AI ad-model training records from 2021 and two internal documents with employee details were also in the dump
summary: Cybernews says it found about 99,100 AI ad-model training records from 2021 (mostly embedding vectors) and two internal documents, a data-use agreement and a warehouse access questionnaire, each with employee details.
detail: We do not repeat the employee details. Android Headlines says it does not know what the two documents are about beyond that. Samsung has not confirmed any of this.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Cybernews researchers examined the files; Samsung has not confirmed the contents.

summary: No source says Samsung's own systems were broken into. Samsung's statement places the incident at a third-party vendor that supported Samsung Ads data processing.
detail: Samsung says the vendor's early investigation indicates 'some Samsung information may have been affected' and that scope is still being worked out. DailySecu says it is not confirmed whether Samsung's own systems were hacked or data leaked.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Samsung points to a vendor; no outlet reports evidence of access to Samsung's own systems.

claim_text: Which vendor it was and how the attacker got in
summary: Samsung has not named the vendor or said how the attacker got in. No technical write-up has been found.
detail: No outlet names a vendor or a method.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source gives a vendor name or method.

claim_text: n0n has listed other large companies, including Expedia, per Cybernews
summary: Cybernews says n0n appeared in mid-September, has listed victims including Visa, Mastercard, Walmart, JPMorgan and Starbucks, and recently leaked over 500MB of Expedia customer data. Samsung's statement does not mention any other company.
detail: These are Cybernews's descriptions of the group's own claims and are not confirmed here. See the separate Expedia report on this site for what Expedia has said.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One outlet's summary of the group's listings; none confirmed by the companies in these sources.

claim_text: A different ransomware group, HYFLOCK, claimed on Nov 22 that it took 1TB of data from "Samsung Group"
summary: KPI News reports that HYFLOCK posted a claim on Nov 22, per two threat-intel trackers, saying it got into "Samsung Group" systems, took 1TB and encrypted systems. KPI News says none of it has been independently checked.
detail: KPI News says it is unclear which Samsung company or overseas unit is meant, what the data is, or whether personal data is involved. It does not link the claim to the Samsung Ads vendor case, and no source we found does. Samsung has not commented on it in any source we found. We do not repeat the technical details in the group's post, and we did not visit the leak page.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: An established Korean outlet reports the group's claim and says it is unverified; the claim is the group's, not a fact.

claim_text: Multicampus, a Samsung SDS subsidiary, had a separate data leak from its online training platform on Nov 9
summary: KPI News reports unauthorized access to Multicampus's staff-training platform on Nov 9, affecting about 70,000 people's names, contact and work details, reported to Korea's privacy regulator on Nov 11.
detail: KPI News says the exact count was not settled at the time. No source ties it to the Samsung Ads vendor case or to either ransomware claim.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One established Korean outlet reports the company notice and regulator report; we found no Multicampus or regulator page to cite.
